A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OPT-OUT and ELUDe. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and sufficiently complete to match retained, relocated, and added material.

before.justification: v2 reports original unlearning experiments, utility evaluations, attack tests, ablations, and human evaluation of ELUDe.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds original TOFU experiments in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The NPO loss, retention loss, and Sliced Wasserstein regularization remain unchanged (v2 Equation 8; v3 Equation 7). The proxy-set reformulation and additional benchmark do not establish a different unlearning procedure.

E1.justification: v3 newly evaluates fictitious-author unlearning on TOFU, previously only cited, including its Retain Set, Real Authors, and World Facts subsets. This extends the retained ELUDe and utility-benchmark coverage to a controlled setting with an exact-unlearning reference.

E2.justification: Appendix E newly uses a model described as an exact-unlearning reference to compare truth-ratio distributions. Table 7 otherwise reuses GA+RT, DPO+RT, NPO+RT, and IDK+RT; comparator membership in existing experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added TOFU experiment uses a 5% forget setting, KS-test-based FQ*, and RQ* aggregating nine metric values across three subsets. Existing ELUDe splits, metrics, model configurations, and training settings remain unchanged; no protocol revision explains the changed human-evaluation scores.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a supplementary analysis of training and inference time and memory complexity, examining SWD overhead. This is analytical rather than measured timing evidence. Existing distance-metric ablations, neighboring-data ablations, and attack analyses retain the same evidence.

E5.justification: v3 introduces Kolmogorov–Smirnov p-values as FQ* for the TOFU distribution comparison. Existing MIA mean/std reporting is unchanged despite relocation, and no new seed information or repeated-run counts are reported.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds a controlled-reference comparison across both models: OPT-OUT reports FQ*=86.6 for each, with RQ*=40.6 for Llama and 45.9 for Phi. All six human-evaluation values in Table 4 change, including forget relevance 85.7 to 89.0 and retain factuality 100.0 to 98.5. Existing ELUDe, utility, attack, and ablation results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 reformulates entity-specific forget and retain sets as proxy subsets. Appendix C adds complexity expressions and scaling arguments, including OPT-OUT training time O(3L^2 + L log L). Existing optimal-transport and SWD mathematics remain unchanged apart from equation numbering.

C1.justification: The introduction newly frames Wikipedia-entity experiments as a testbed toward practical privacy unlearning and explicitly acknowledges that actual private-user data are not studied. This qualifies applicability while retaining the abstract and conclusion's principal dataset, method, and outperformance claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of proxy coverage and privacy applicability, but replaces v2's explicit retention-degradation limitation with the Wikipedia-data caveat. Appendix C newly argues that overhead remains manageable. Appendix E claims consistent TOFU superiority despite Table 7 showing Llama RQ*=40.6 for OPT-OUT versus 47.7 for DPO+RT.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds reference-model forward-pass accounting and describes a small random-projection layer for SWD without specifying its dimension. Appendix A's hyperparameters, three-epoch budget, four H100 GPUs, and existing code/data access and prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Ma et al. (2024), already discussed as concurrent work in v2, now explicitly supplies the proxy-set framework adopted in Section 3.1. The cited-work set otherwise remains unchanged; RWKU's preprint-to-conference update is bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Targeted rewriting expands the problem definition and revises the introduction and limitations. v3 adds acknowledgements and two appendix sections, reletters existing appendices, and updates Daniel Rim's affiliation. Most wording and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to compare instance-level and entity-level unlearning. The MIA table moves from the back matter into the main text, and complexity and TOFU tables are added. Other plots and appendix examples are retained, with localized reflow and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added TOFU comparison and explicit proxy-data boundaries provide a modest net gain in validation and scope clarity. Benefits are limited by the TOFU superiority claim overlooking lower Llama retention, removal of the retention-loss caveat, and a cost argument that does not explain how parameter-space SWD overhead acquires its stated dependence on sequence length.
